title: Article 70 — Discharge of President’s functions in other contingencies

content.overview: Article 70 provides that Parliament may make such provision as it thinks fit for the discharge of the functions of the President in any contingency not provided for in Chapter I of Part V.
content.glance: Parliament may by law provide for discharge of Presidential functions in contingencies not covered by Chapter I of Part V.
content.study:
Article 70 is a residual enabling provision. Articles 65 and related provisions cover vacancy and inability; Article 70 allows Parliament to legislate for other unprovided contingencies.

Examination: residual parliamentary power; supplements Arts 65 etc.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Parliament may make provision for the discharge of the functions of the President in any contingency not provided for in this Chapter.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 70 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 70 provides that Parliament may make such provision as it thinks fit for the discharge of the functions of the President in any contingency not provided for in Chapter I of Part V of the Constitution.

examTips: Residual parliamentary power for uncovered Presidential contingencies.

keyTakeaways: Art 70: Parliament may provide for uncovered Presidential contingencies.
